title: Maximum residue levels for dodine
summary: EU proposes increase in MRL for dodine on grapes
update: The European Union (EU) is proposing to increase the maximum residue level (MRL) for dodine on grapes from 0.01 to 2 mg/kg.
what_changing: The EU is proposing to increase the MRL for dodine on table grapes and wine grapes from the limit of determination (LOD) of 0.01 mg/kg to 2 mg/kg. (The LOD is the lowest level that can be detected using the most modern and reliable analytical methods.)
why: Following an application for a change of MRL by the producer of dodine, the European Food Safety Authority evaluated the request and concluded that increasing the MRL would not pose a risk for consumers ( EFSA 2025 ).
timeline: The Regulation is expected to be published in October 2026, and will apply 6 months after publication.
background: MRLs are set in accordance with the rules set out in Regulation 396/2005 . For information on current MRLs for other substances, please consult the EU Pesticide Residues database . For further information on the setting of import tolerances, see Pesticide residue import tolerance MRLs explained .
resources: EFSA (2025) Modification of the existing maximum residue level for dodine in grapes . EFSA Journal, 23(11): e9757.
